DIS.rationale: Disney presents a moderately attractive fundamental profile anchored by a durable franchise with improving economics. The operating business is healthy: Q2 FY2026 revenue grew +6.5% YoY to $25.17B, operating income expanded +3.6% YoY to $4.60B, and operating margins held at 18.3%. The Experiences segment — the franchise anchor generating ~68% of total segment operating income — delivered 7% YoY revenue growth and $2.6B in operating income. Streaming has inflected toward profitability with DTC operating income jumping from $143M to $1.3B in FY2025, and Q2 FY2026 streaming revenue grew 13% YoY. The balance sheet is improving: total equity grew +8.0% over five quarters to $115.31B while liabilities were flat, and debt-to-equity declined from 0.85x to 0.78x. Operating cash flow was robust at $6.91B in Q2. Valuation is compelling vs own history: trailing P/E of 14.3x sits in the bottom quartile of its 12.5x–23.8x 365-day range, P/B of 1.53x is at the floor of its 1.5x–2.1x range, and the 7.0% earnings yield provides a ~253bp spread over the 10-year Treasury at 4.47%. The stock is -20.3% off its 52-week high of $124.69. The primary concern is the -29.8% YoY EPS decline (to $1.27) despite operating income growth, pointing to non-operating charges (likely elevated interest expense given rising rates) eroding the operating improvement. This gap limits conviction in the 'cheap' P/E reading. Near-term catalysts include Q2 earnings beat ($1.57 EPS vs $1.49 consensus), management's FY2026 guidance of 12% adjusted EPS growth with double-digit FY2027 growth, the $8B buyback commitment, June content catalysts (NBA Finals, Toy Story 5, Avatar: Fire and Ash on Disney+), and the Canadian streaming levy suspension removing an international cost headwind. The Paramount-WBD mega-merger and FCC regulatory scrutiny on ABC stations represent offsetting risks. Score of +0.35 reflects solid fundamentals and attractive valuation partially tempered by the net income compression and regulatory/competitive overhangs.
